correctness.rationale: The known ladder total-three-cut wedge formula in arXiv:2408.07646 Theorem 3.3 concentrates rational homology in even degree 2n-6. Reduced equivariant Hopf trace gives a complement sum over invariant induced subsets with independence number at most 2, necessarily size ≤4 by bipartiteness. Four exhaustive orbit cases, with parity subcases, produce traces (B,(-1)^n B,h,(-1)^n h). Ordinary rational C2×C2 character theory proves the module is the stated twisted square-pair permutation representation. Exact independent finite orbit traces n=3..40, oriented direct chain traces n=3..7 and full reduced mod-two ranks n=3..6 corroborate. No computational extrapolation is used for infinite n.

originality.rationale: The new claim concerns the entire rational ladder automorphism representation and its row-exchange parity twist, not the known homotopy type and Betti number. Primary full texts arXiv:2209.13503, arXiv:2408.07646 and arXiv:2407.08158 and targeted published-result-index comparisons do not supply equivalent all-parameter character formulas. A separate previously reported finite 4×4-grid character and several fixed total-cut examples do not imply the ladder statement. An unindexed equivalent remains a genuine risk.
residual_risks: No search is a proof of uniqueness; a less-indexed equivalent equivariant ladder formula may exist.
The first two arXiv sources were consulted from their available full-text PDF revisions; verified first-public posting dates, rather than revision dates, were used for chronological classification.

value.rationale: For the natural infinite family of all two-row ladders, this recovers the full symmetry-sensitive rational top-homology representation, going strictly beyond previously known wedge counts. The parity-dependent row-swap scalar and simple combinatorial square-pair action give structural information and explicit eigenspace multiplicities. The theorem addresses the exact symmetry action singled out by the already studied total-cut filtration, rather than an arbitrary finite numerical slice.
